statement_summary: Program meets the HIPAA Security Rule and is documented
Security Officer designated in writing
Annual enterprise risk analysis covering devices, OT, vendors, and AI
Risk acceptance authority by level; no patient-safety risk accepted above Low
Quarterly reporting to the audit committee
Annual review of policies and standards
Written, risk-rated, time-limited exceptions
Sanctions, including medical staff bylaws for physicians
No BAA, no PHI; purchasing gate
Annual reassessment of Tier 1 vendors
Security review before buying or connecting a networked medical device
Annual independent evaluation
6-year retention of security documentation
AI tools approved before use; 92.210 identification and mitigation
Cyber hazards and an IT outage annex in the emergency plan
Unique accounts; generic accounts only for view-only kiosks
Role-based, least-privilege access with approval
MFA for remote, external EHR, and all administrator access
Sponsors and end dates for all non-employee accounts; monthly reconciliation
regulatory_driver: C-HPH-R01 (164.308(a)(3)(ii)(C)); C-HPH-R08 (CPG Essential: Revoke Credentials for Departing Workforce Members)

statement_summary: Same-day removal for terminations, including badges and shared credentials
Transfers remove prior roles
Quarterly access reviews, including privileged and practice users
Privileged access through privileged access management; 2 standing break-glass admins only
Vendor remote access only through the vendor access platform with MFA and recording
Vault and rotate service and vendor passwords; no default credentials
Sealed break-glass accounts per critical system, tested quarterly
Screen lock and EHR session timeouts
Behavior-based EHR access analytics reviewed monthly
Affiliated practice users limited to their own and shared patients
Incident response plan with two runbooks, reviewed annually
Immediate reporting; no discipline for good-faith reports
Discovery and determination dates recorded
Severity 1 declared within 30 minutes; crisis team within 2 hours
Decision log with four-factor assessment for every PHI incident
Cyber incidents affecting care activate the Hospital Incident Command System and the IT outage annex
Downtime procedures for 72 hours, drilled quarterly
Diversion criteria, decision makers, and log
Out-of-band contact tree and alternate means on every unit
Ransom decision rules with sanctions check
Notices follow the P08 matrix and are approved by counsel
Device-related deaths and serious injuries reported within 10 work days
Restore in BIA order; rebuild compromised systems
Annual exercise; may serve as the 482.15 additional exercise
Lessons learned within 14 days; report within 30 days
Data owners classify data; default to Restricted
Encrypt Restricted data at rest and in transit
Unencryptable devices on restricted networks and inventoried
Sanitization or destruction certificate before any device leaves
No production PHI in test environments
Restricted data only in approved AI tools with a no-training BAA
Encrypted, isolated, write-once backups
Paper downtime records handled as Restricted and back-entered within 72 hours
Medical records at least 5 years; security records 6 years
Drug library, dispensing profile, and interface mapping changes approved and monitored
Authorized use of hospital systems
Look up records only with a work reason
No shared passwords or badges; lock or tap out
Report phishing and incidents right away
Training at hire (before activation for non-employees) and yearly
No unapproved software, personal devices on clinical networks, or unknown USB media
PHI sent outside only through approved channels
No PHI in unapproved generative AI tools
Recording only with all-party consent; AI scribes only for approved clinicians
No changes to decision support settings outside committee change control
Screens with PHI out of public view
No bypassing or testing of security controls
